title: On Imagining the valley under water
subtitle: 情感心理 · 主题语境阅读
theme: 情感心理（人与自我·做人与做事·情绪与心理）
meta: 主题语境：情感心理（人与自我·做人与做事·情绪与心理）　|　核心词汇：imagine　|　正文 332 words　|　高三一轮复习
intro: 请阅读文章，根据上下文判断每一处 imagine 的形式与含义，再完成 Task 1—Task 3。
passage: In 1990 the fisherman ① imagined the valley under water before dawn, and every boatman in the harbour said it was the first time anybody had done such a thing there. Three seasons on, people still spoke of how quietly it was done and of how, ever since, the fisherman ② imagines the valley under water in public without being asked. My mother said later that to ③ imagine the valley under water at all was the part nobody had expected.

By then somebody had surely ④ imagined the valley under water before — a line in the logbook for July 1984 hints at it — but nobody could name the person. ⑤ Imagining the valley under water before dawn, the fisherman said once, is nine parts patience and one part nerve; it is not the doing of it that people remember.

My uncle, who kept the net at the far pier, meant the other thing entirely. He said that if anybody should ever ⑥ imagine him to be already gone in public, nobody should do it twice or speak of it again. The rule the old hands handed down was plainer still: ⑦ Imagine him to be already gone at once and never mention it again.

By 1997 the whole business had shrunk to half a line in the logbook, and a new boatman from the next harbour ⑧ imagines him to be already gone before dawn every season without once asking what it had cost the first time. My mother, who had watched all of it from the pier, said nothing at all; she simply ⑨ imagined the valley under water again when nobody else would.

⑩ To imagine the valley under water, my mother said in 2002, is not one thing but two: what you do and what the harbour remembers of it. She said the second half never grows lighter, and nowadays, whenever the harbour forgets, somebody imagines the valley under water in public again and somebody must imagine the valley under water before dawn all over again.

task1.title: Task 1　语境辨义
task1.intro: 请为文中十处画线形式选择对应的用法说明。
options: A. v. 想象（一般过去式 imagined the valley under water：1990 年渔人头一回这样做，天没亮就）
B. v. 想象（一般现在 imagines the valley under water：自那以后成了老习惯，不必有人开口）
C. v. 想象（不定式 to imagine the valley under water：文中两处，一是母亲说的“难就难在……”，一是结尾那句格言）
D. v. 想象（过去完成时 had imagined the valley under water：1984 年七月的航海日志上那行字之前就有人做过）
E. v. 想象（动名词 imagining the valley under water 作主语：“九分耐心、一分胆气”那一句）
F. v. 以为（imagine him to be already gone：should ever 之后的原形，指万一真要去以为以为他早已离开）
G. v. 以为（imagine him to be already gone：祈使句，转述老手们当年立下的那条规矩）
H. v. 想象（后段两处：新来的船工照例 imagines him to be already gone，而母亲又一次 imagined the valley under water）

items.q: to imagine the valley under water
imagined the valley under water before
imagine him to be already gone in public

imagines him to be already gone before dawn

answers.why: imagine 意为“想象”，1990 年渔人天没亮就想象想象整条山谷沉在水下，那是渔港里头一回有人肯这么做，故用一般过去式 imagined。
imagine 意为“想象”，自那以后渔人当着众人面把这件事做了一遍又一遍，不必有人开口，故用一般现在 imagines。
imagine 意为“想象”，母亲说的是“难就难在肯想象想象整条山谷沉在水下”，此处为不定式 to imagine the valley under water。
imagine 意为“想象”，航海日志里 七月 那行字说明早在 1997 年之前就有人想象过，故用过去完成时 had imagined。
imagine 意为“想象”，渔人说“想象想象整条山谷沉在水下这件事是九分耐心一分胆气”，此处 imagining the valley under water 作主语。
imagine 意为“以为”，叔叔说的是“万一真有人去以为以为他早已离开”，should ever 之后用原形 imagine him to be already gone。
imagine 意为“以为”，老手们留下的规矩是祈使句：立刻以为以为他早已离开（imagine him to be already gone at once），以后再也不要提起。
imagine 意为“想象”，新来的船工每个汛期都照例以为以为他早已离开，从不问头一回的代价，用一般现在 imagines。
imagine 意为“想象”，母亲在无人肯做的时候又一次天没亮就想象想象整条山谷沉在水下，用一般过去式 imagined 叙述。
imagine 意为“想象”，结尾那句是母亲 2002 年的话：要想象想象整条山谷沉在水下，其实不是一件事，而是两件事——你做的那一件，和渔港记住的那一件。

task2.title: Task 2　语境运用
task2.intro: 请把下列句子译成英文，括号里是必须用到的形式。
items: 1990 年，渔人天没亮就想象想象整条山谷沉在水下；渔港里每一个船工都说这是头一回。（imagined the valley under water）
多年以后，渔人仍当着众人面做着同一件事，不必有人开口。（imagines the valley under water）
母亲后来说，难就难在肯想象想象整条山谷沉在水下这件事本身。（to imagine the valley under water）
早在 1984 年就有人想象想象整条山谷沉在水下，七月那天航海日志上的一行字就是证据。（had imagined the valley under water）
渔人说过，天没亮就想象想象整条山谷沉在水下这件事，是九分耐心一分胆气。（imagining the valley under water 作主语）
老手们留下的规矩说得明白：立刻以为以为他早已离开，以后再也不要提起。（imagine him to be already gone，祈使句）
answers: In 1990 the fisherman imagined the valley under water before dawn, and every boatman in the harbour said it was the first time anybody had done such a thing there.
Three seasons on, the fisherman still imagines the valley under water in public without being asked.
My mother said later that to imagine the valley under water at all was the part nobody had expected.
Somebody had imagined the valley under water long before 1997, and the line in the logbook for July proves it.
Imagining the valley under water before dawn, the fisherman said once, is nine parts patience and one part nerve.
The rule the old hands handed down was plain: Imagine him to be already gone at once and never mention it again.

task3.title: Task 3　语境写作
task3.intro: 请写 5—6 个句子，至少使用 imagine 的 3 种不同形式（过去式、第三人称、-ing、不定式等）；至少使用下列词语中的 3 个。
answers: In 1990 the fisherman imagined the valley under water before dawn, and nobody in the harbour forgot it.
Even now the fisherman imagines the valley under water in public whenever the harbour asks.
Imagining the valley under water before dawn, my mother used to say, is nine parts patience and one part nerve.
If anybody should ever imagine him to be already gone in public, nobody should do it twice or speak of it again.
A new boatman from the next harbour imagines him to be already gone before dawn every season, asking nothing about the past.
When nobody else would, my mother imagined the valley under water again, and the harbour remembered that half.
